html:
On 27 April 1993 a Zambian military plane carrying the national football team to a World Cup qualifier in Senegal crashed into the sea off Libreville, Gabon, killing all 30 people on board, including 18 players.

The team was one of the best in Africa. The captain, Kalusha Bwalya, was not on the plane because he was travelling from Europe, and he led a rebuilt team that reached the final of the Africa Cup of Nations in 1994.

The dead were buried near the national stadium in Lusaka. In 2012 Zambia won the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time, in Libreville itself, near the crash site, a moment that moved the whole of Zambia.
sum: On 27 April 1993 a Zambian military plane carrying the national football team to a World Cup qualifier in Senegal crashed into the sea off Libreville, Gabon, killing all 30 people on board, including 18 players.
